
{{Short description|German physicist}}
{{Third-party|date=June 2026}}

'''Marius Grundmann''' (born 14 November 1964 in [[Berlin]]) is a German physicist and university professor. He served as Director of the Felix Bloch Institute for Solid State Physics for two decades.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marius Grundmann |url=https://www.tech-europe.org/speaker/marius-grundmann |website=Tech Tour Europe |access-date=23 June 2026}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Grundmann attended primary school in Berlin-Schmargendorf from 1970 to 1974. He then attended the Gymnasium zum Grauen Kloster, where he obtained his ''Abitur'' (German university entrance qualification) in 1982.<ref name="CV">{{cite web
 |url=https://home.uni-leipzig.de/grundm/grundmann_cv_d.pdf
 |title=Curriculum Vitae – Prof. Dr. Marius Grundmann
 |publisher=Leipzig University
 |language=de
 |access-date=9 June 2026
}}</ref> In 1983, he began studying physics at the [[Technical University of Berlin]]. He graduated in 1988 with a diploma thesis entitled ''Pseudomorphic Quantum Wells and Excitonic Effects'', receiving the overall grade of ''sehr gut'' ("very good").<ref name="CV" /> In 1984, he was awarded a scholarship by the [[German National Academic Foundation]] (''Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes'').<ref name="CV" /> From 1988 to 1991, he pursued doctoral studies at the Technical University of Berlin under the supervision of Dieter Bimberg. He completed his doctorate with a dissertation on ''Heteroepitaxy of InP on Si'', graduating ''summa cum laude''.<ref name="CV" /> Following research appointments in the United States, Grundmann held a postdoctoral habilitation fellowship funded by the [[German Research Foundation]] (DFG) from 1992 to 1994.<ref name="CV" /> From 1994 to 2000, he worked as a senior research engineer at the Institute for Solid State Physics of the Technical University of Berlin. He completed his [[habilitation]] in 1995 and was granted the ''[[venia legendi]]'' in 1996.<ref name="CV" />

From 2000 to 2004, Grundmann was funded through the Heisenberg Programme of the German Research Foundation (DFG).<ref>{{cite web |title=Physik |url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/projekt/5251478 |website=GEPRIS |publisher=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) |language=de |access-date=23 June 2026}}</ref> In the same year, he was appointed professor at [[Leipzig University]].<ref name="CV" /> Since 2002, he has been director of the Institute of Experimental Physics II at Leipzig University.<ref name="CV" /> In 2021, he co-founded SAXON Q, a Leipzig-based [[quantum computing]] company developing room-temperature quantum computers based on [[nitrogen-vacancy center]]s in diamond.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://business-saxony.com/en/news-events/news/news-detail/n1797-millionen-investition-in-skalierbares-quantencomputing-aus-sachsen
 |title=Millions invested in scalable quantum computing from Saxony
 |publisher=Business Saxony
 |access-date=9 June 2026
}}</ref> From 2022 to 2025, he served as dean of the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences at Leipzig University.<ref name="CV" />

== Selected publications ==

* ''The Physics of Semiconductors: An Introduction Including Nanophysics and Applications'' (''Graduate Texts in Physics''). Springer International Publishing, Cham, 2021. ISBN 978-3-030-51568-3. doi:[https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-51569-0 10.1007/978-3-030-51569-0].
* Marius Grundmann (ed.), ''Nano-Optoelectronics'' (''NanoScience and Technology''). Springer, Berlin and Heidelberg, 2002. ISBN 3-642-62807-9. doi:[https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-56149-8 10.1007/978-3-642-56149-8].

== Honors and awards ==
* 1998 – Gerhard Hess Prize of the [[German Research Foundation]] (DFG).<ref name="CV" />
* 1998 – [[Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Prize]], awarded jointly by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and the [[Federal Ministry of Education and Research]] (BMBF).<ref name="CV" />
* 2011 – Leipzig Science Prize of the [[Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name="LWP">{{cite web
 |url=https://www.leipzig.de/newsarchiv/news/leipziger-wissenschaftspreis-2011-an-prof-dr-marius-grundmann-verliehen
 |title=Leipziger Wissenschaftspreis 2011 an Prof. Dr. Marius Grundmann verliehen
 |publisher=Stadt Leipzig
 |language=de
 |access-date=23 July 2026
}}</ref>
* 2020 – Rudolf Jaeckel Prize of the German Vacuum Society (DVG).<ref name="DVG">{{cite web
 |url=https://pro-physik.de/nachrichten/rudolf-jaeckel-preis-2020-fuer-marius-grundmann
 |title=Rudolf-Jaeckel-Preis 2020 für Marius Grundmann
 |publisher=pro-physik

 |access-date=23 July 2026
}}</ref>
